subdomain: 5.2 Identify risks, limitations, and failure modes of LLM systems

en.question: A retrieval-augmented assistant recommends a repair procedure. Its citation supports the component's identity but says nothing about the recommended operating temperature. Company policy permits procedural recommendations only when every safety-critical parameter is supported by approved documentation. Which behavior best handles this evidence gap?

options.text: Publish the recommendation because the cited document is genuine and identifies the correct component family.
options.note: A genuine source can support one claim while leaving another unsupported. Document existence does not establish the safety-critical temperature parameter.

options.text: Withhold the procedure pending approved evidence for its temperature, or escalate the unresolved parameter.
options.note: Claim-level support is required by the policy, so partial grounding cannot authorize the procedure. Abstention preserves the distinction between verified identity and an unverified operating condition.

options.text: Generate several temperatures and use the median, retaining the original component citation beside the result.
options.note: Aggregation of generated values creates no approved documentary support. Reusing the identity citation would misleadingly imply evidence for the temperature.

options.text: Publish the recommendation with a disclaimer that retrieved documents may not contain every implementation detail.
options.note: A disclaimer acknowledges the gap but does not satisfy the explicit support requirement. The unsupported safety-critical parameter would still be recommended.

references.title: NIST AI 600-1: Generative Artificial Intelligence Profile
